display.title: The Rebbe Rashab and the Amazing Dream
display.summary_short: A Shabbos-observant doctor in Vitebsk dreams of a red-bearded tzaddik telling him to travel to save a life, then meets the Rebbe Rashab and recognizes him.
display.summary_long: The storyteller opens with the Rebbe's words that in the past the Rebbeim gave brachos to those who asked, but now they give without being asked; we only need to receive them by following the Rebbe's instructions. A Rebbe also reminds us that a doctor is Hashem's messenger, and Hashem is the true Healer. The Rebbe Rashab would often send the sick to Dr. Lieberman in Vitebsk, a G-d-fearing doctor who taught Ein Yaakov and avoided traveling on Shabbos. One Shabbos afternoon he dreams of a man with deep eyes and a red beard who tells him that to save a life one must travel even on Shabbos. He wakes, washes negel vasser (the storyteller explains the halachah for a daytime nap), and finds a farmer begging him to come to his critically ill daughter. He goes, and with Hashem's help she recovers. Later, called to a patient in Lubavitch, he visits the Rebbe Rashab and freezes: the Rebbe is the man from his dream. The Rebbe Rashab says only that he had sent the farmer to him weeks before. The doctor becomes a devoted Chassid.
display.lesson: The Rebbeim give brachos even without being asked; we receive them by following their instructions. Also: wash negel vasser after any sleep, by the bed at night and at the sink after a daytime nap.
